headline: 88% done and in the final stretch — the closing rap albums are rebalancing the chart, pulling trap tempos and vocals back up, though house keeps its overall lead.
insights: 88% (2,858 tracks), ~15m to go. The run is into the last alphabetical stretch — Vultures 2, Whole Lotta Red, Yeezus, We Don't Trust You — the pure-rap tail of the library.

Trap is fighting back. The 130–150 BPM range grew from 352 → 496 tracks as the rap albums landed, and 136/143 BPM re-entered the top-four tempo spikes. House still leads (829 vs 496) but the gap narrowed from 2:1 toward ~1.7:1.
Vocal share ticked back up 0.956 → 0.962 — the rap closers are re-weighting the (over-firing) vocal metric upward after the instrumental-house dip. Predictable and consistent.

Aggregate character barely moved across the last 600 tracks: energy 0.54, danceability 0.34, major-key share 34% (979 of 2,867). Both halves of the library — album and Singles — are now fully and evenly represented.

Throughput eased to 21.6/min — the big closing FLAC albums are heavier to decode — ETA ~15m. Just 3 decode failures in 2,861 (0.10%): Huncho Jack 'Eye 2 Eye', Max Dean 'Gets Like That', Thank Me Later 'The Resistance'.
The dashboard-hang bug is fixed (WAL mode) and holding — polls back to ~0.07s. On completion the pipeline auto-classifies, arc-sequences, pushes all playlists to the device, and pings.
